segments.title: 第121章 徐有漁之父
segments.content:
The rock club's performance came to a perfect conclusion amidst the duet of Li Luo and Yan Zhusheng.

Yuan Wanqing squinted, her gaze falling on Li Luo, who was standing close to her daughter.

However, Li Luo hadn't really done anything; it was Yan Zhusheng who had pressed herself against him.

Especially during the climax of the chorus in the latter half, Li Luo had already moved half a step away, completely yielding the microphone to Yan Zhusheng.

But Yan Zhusheng had taken the microphone off its stand and proactively held it to Li Luo's lips.

Yuan Wanqing couldn't really say much about it.

As for Ying Chanxi on the other side, her expression had already returned to calm.

When the music ended and applause erupted all around, she also smiled and clapped. At a glance, no one would notice anything unusual.

"That was a really great performance. It's a good thing there was another microphone." Xu Youyu sighed, then praised, "Li Luo's on-the-spot reaction was quite fast. He didn't look flustered at all. He's really a big-hearted performer."

"Mmm." Ying Chanxi nodded lightly, her thoughts unknown.

"After this is over, remember to come for lunch," Xu Youyu said with a smile, patting Ying Chanxi's shoulder. "My mom went home to cook right after the parent-teacher conference. No need to trouble Li Luo's parents. We can just have them come over to my place as guests in a bit."

"Is that so?" Ying Chanxi was taken aback for a moment. "I remember your home is at..."

"In the faculty apartments of Qianjiang University." Xu Youyu blinked. "Let's meet at the school gate in a bit. I'll take you there."

"Okay, I'll let Uncle and Auntie know."

"Remember to invite Yan Zhusheng's mom too," Xu Youyu told her. "I'll go tell Li Luo as well."

Ying Chanxi nodded and walked straight toward Lin Xiuhong, showing no intention of going to the second-floor activity room to find Li Luo.

Qianjiang University, School of Liberal Arts office.

Professor Xu Rongsheng of the literature department leaned back in his office chair, wearing a pair of gold-rimmed glasses, and checked his email.

He clicked on a letter from the Provincial Writers' Association. It was a seminar invitation, asking Professor Xu Rongsheng to provide guidance at the seminar on jointly promoting the development of online literature, to be held by the Provincial Online Writers' Association in early February this year.

Xu Rongsheng raised his eyebrows. He was noncommittal about online literature. His main research area was modern and contemporary literature, which had a tenuous connection to the ancestors of online literature.

Moreover, he was already a presidium member of the Provincial Writers' Association, so they would always be prioritized for invitations to various internal seminars.

At the same time, for such invited seminars, attendees would receive a corresponding stipend, and normal expenses during the meeting would also be covered by the association.

It was basically a free trip.

However, this seminar was spearheaded by the Provincial Online Writers' Association, which was just established this year. It was the association's first attempt to gather authors offline under an official banner.

Its significance was quite profound.

The preliminary dates for this seminar were from February 6th to 9th, for a total of three and a half days.

The lecture fee they offered Xu Rongsheng was 5000 yuan per day, along with free accommodation and meals.

To be honest, Xu Rongsheng didn't consider himself a very well-known professor. He was usually just a figurehead at the Writers' Association.

In the past, when invited by the association, there sometimes wasn't even a stipend, only free accommodation.

This Provincial Online Writers' Association was quite generous, actually offering him a stipend plan of 5000 yuan per day, which was quite rare.

After all, he wasn't like those professors from finance or medical schools who could often participate in commercial conferences. A stipend of this amount was quite rare for a literature professor.

So, he was naturally tempted.

Xu Rongsheng looked at his schedule for the rest of the year; he didn't have much going on in February for the time being.

Mid-February was New Year's Eve. The 6th to the 9th... that would be a good time to relax and earn some extra money.

With this in mind, Xu Rongsheng carefully worded a reply to the Provincial Writers' Association, stating that he could participate in the seminar in February.

Just then, his phone rang.

Xu Rongsheng answered the call and heard his wife on the other end:

"Old Xu, your daughter brought classmates home today, along with their parents."

"Isn't today the parent-teacher conference? And since Youyu is renting a room at someone else's place, I thought I'd invite their parents over for a meal."

"Remember to come back a little earlier for lunch to host them."

Xu Rongsheng acknowledged, then asked, "Which classmates' parents?"

"They seem to be from the first year." His wife, Cui Suling, said on the other end, "Two of the kids live with her, and there's another girl she's been getting along well with recently. We probably haven't met any of them."

"Alright, I got it," Xu Rongsheng said with a nod. "I'll head back as soon as I'm done here."

After hanging up, Xu Rongsheng finished reading the emails in his inbox, took care of the matters within, glanced at the time, then stood up, tidied his desk, grabbed his coat, and headed for the faculty apartments.

On the other side, Li Luo's group was also gathering at the school gate.

After finding Yuan Wanqing, Yan Zhusheng quietly walked to her mother's side, tugged on her sleeve, and whispered in her ear:

"The very cute one is Ying Chanxi, the one with the big chest is Xu Youyu, and that one is Li Luo."

"They are all my good friends."

Yan Zhusheng's introduction was very direct, and Yuan Wanqing immediately remembered the other two girls, greeting them with a smile.

Ying Chanxi and Xu Youyu also responded politely.

Seeing that everyone had arrived, Xu Youyu said with a smile, "Well then, Uncle and Auntie, please follow me. My home is in the faculty apartments of Qianjiang University. It's just a few minutes' walk from here."

At this time, Yan Zhusheng was obediently following beside Yuan Wanqing, walking at the very back of the group.

Ahead were Li Guohong and Lin Xiuhong, with Ying Chanxi accompanying Lin Xiuhong.

Li Luo walked beside Xu Youyu, heading toward Qianjiang University.

After hearing what Xu Youyu said, Li Guohong asked curiously, "Do your parents work at Qianjiang University?"

"Yes, my dad is a professor in the School of Liberal Arts." Xu Youyu nodded. "My mom is a librarian. She usually works at the school library, so it's a pretty relaxed job."

This was considered a perk for professors' families; any cushy positions at the university were prioritized for them.

"We've really troubled your mother today," Lin Xiuhong said helplessly. "We were originally planning to buy some groceries and have a meal at our place."

"Uncle and Auntie, you attended the first-year parent-teacher conference, which takes longer to get through," Xu Youyu explained. "My mom's second-year conference ended earlier, so she could go back and cook. This way, we can eat as soon as we get there."

"Then next time we have a chance, we'll invite your parents over for a meal."

"No problem."

The group walked across the intersection, turned north at the corner, and headed toward the residential community built along the river.

"Before we go to your place, let's buy something first." When they passed by a fruit shop, Li Luo, who was walking at the front, stopped and walked right into the store. "We should bring something when visiting."

"Why are you being so polite?" Xu Youyu quickly followed him in, laughing in spite of herself. "Let me choose, we can just buy something simple."

"We should bring something," Lin Xiuhong nodded. "Li Luo is being thoughtful. You should buy a bit more."

Based on the information in his memory, Li Luo picked some mangoes and a pineapple, as well as a small bag of green grapes, and asked the shop owner to pack them up.

Xu Youyu, who had originally wanted to help pick out the fruit, looked at the fruits Li Luo had chosen and fell into a deep thought for a moment.

"How did you know my parents like to eat these?"

Her mother, Cui Suling, loved mangoes and pineapples, while her father was fond of green grapes because you didn't have to spit out the skin after washing them, which was more convenient.

"Huh?" Li Luo was taken aback for a second, then feigned a coincidental smile. "Maybe my parents and I just have similar tastes."

Finished speaking, Li Luo asked the owner, "How much?"

"80 yuan and 4 mao."

"Round it off, boss."

"Alright, eighty."

"Mom!" Li Luo called out to Lin Xiuhong. "Time to pay!"

"You little rascal." Lin Xiuhong shot him a look, walked over, took out a 100-yuan bill, and handed it to the owner. "Didn't you bring any cash?"

"I did," Li Luo said with an innocent look on his face. "But a penny saved is a penny earned. I'm very frugal."

"I can't tell if you're frugal, but you're certainly thick-skinned." Lin Xiuhong watched as Li Luo took the 20 yuan change from the owner without batting an eye and chuckled. "If you put this little bit of cleverness into your studies, you might actually see some improvement."

"Being 27th in the whole school still isn't enough to satisfy you?"

"Well, Chanxi is still always number one. Why don't you learn from her?"

"I'm afraid she'll cry if I take first place, hiss..." Just as Li Luo finished speaking, his foot was stepped on. "Mom, Ying Chanxi stepped on me."

"I didn't see anything." Lin Xiuhong looped her arm through Ying Chanxi's and walked out of the fruit shop with a bright smile. "Let's go, Chanxi. We'll ignore him."

As she walked out of the fruit shop with Lin Xiuhong, Ying Chanxi turned her head back and stuck her small, pink tongue out at Li Luo with a blank expression before quickly turning back, as if nothing had happened.

"Why do I get the feeling you're not their biological son?" Xu Youyu snickered from the side. "More like you were picked out of a trash can."

"Don't laugh, Xuejie. If it weren't for you being in the second year and me in the first, your number one spot in the grade would have been in jeopardy sooner or later."

"Heh." Upon hearing this, Xu Youyu lightly stepped on his other foot and caught up to Lin Xiuhong and Ying Chanxi ahead. "Bring the fruit."

(End of Chapter)
